## Mirror a reflecting wall (`reflecting`) {#sec-ch11-reflecting}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0
status: draft
-->

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
Mirror cell values across the wall and reverse the normal momentum or velocity row. Scalars retain even parity.
Default: reflecting on external faces.
Order: exact discrete operation or local derivation below; coupled solver order not measured.
:::

### Derivation

Use only cell averages here. At a Cartesian lower wall let the first owned cell have index $i$ and let
$l=1,\ldots,n_g$ count ghost depth. Integrating an even extension of a scalar over each reflected cell gives
its matching owned-cell average. Integrating an odd extension of normal velocity gives the negative average.
For an orthogonal wall, density is even and normal momentum is odd, so their ratio has the same odd parity.
Thus the callback implements

$$
\begin{aligned}
q_{i-l}&=q_{i+l-1},\\
v_{1,i-l}&=-v_{1,i+l-1}.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch11-reflecting-parity}

Here $q$ is any even component and $v_1$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.
The upper-wall mapping reverses the last owned slab in the same way. `reflecting_inner` ([`bc_func.cpp:10-34`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L10-L34))
implements @eq-ch11-reflecting-parity with a flip and a sign change of row `4-dim`.
At a symmetry-preserving Riemann interface, equal densities and opposite normal velocities give zero normal
mass flux by reflection symmetry. This argument does not supply a hydrostatic pressure continuation or a
proof for arbitrary nonorthogonal component conventions. C1 verifies the exact discrete parity and idempotence.

The report-only checks are `src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.py`; their current output is
`src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.out`. They do not call a snapy kernel.

### Numerical method

The input remains in its supplied representation. Conserved and primitive calls negate the designated
normal row; `kScalar` only mirrors. Collapsed directions return immediately. The fill precedes reconstruction
through the stage ordering in @sec-ch11-timing. Odd/even extension is exact for symmetric data; no measured
wall convergence order is available here.

@fig-ch11-reflecting-stencil illustrates the operations, with labelled roles independent of colour.

```{python}

#| fig-cap: "Mirror a reflecting wall. Schematic only; no simulation measurements."
```

: Implementation sites for reflecting. {#tbl-ch11-reflecting-code}

1. Return for a collapsed direction, then copy and reverse the adjacent owned slab. The anchor `reflecting_inner` is in [`bc_func.cpp:10-34`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L10-L34).
2. Negate the normal row for conserved or primitive input; retain even parity for scalar input. The anchor `reflecting_inner` is in [`bc_func.cpp:10-34`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L10-L34).
3. Repeat on exchange-owned tangential corner slabs when requested by the block exchange path. The anchor `refresh` is in [`meshblock.cpp:951-978`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L951-L978).

### Limits

A mirror of the total state is not a continuation of a stratified equilibrium. The reference-state
procedure in @sec-ch11-wb addresses that distinction. Reflection alone does not establish the accuracy of
wall diffusion coefficients or nonorthogonal momentum treatment.

Untested switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix. No new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver result is claimed.
